title: ‘दसैँ’ र ‘सहीको सही’ कथामा वर्गीय शक्तिसम्बन्ध
nepali: गाउँको सन्देश (२०१०) कथासङ्ग्रहमा सङ्गृहीत ‘दसैँ’ र ‘सहीको सही’ कथामा तत्कालीन सामन्ती संरचनायुक्त समाजमा विद्यमान उच्चवर्गीय र निम्नवर्गीय चिन्तन, सोच, चरित्र र तिनका व्यवहारको प्रतिनिधित्व गराई निम्नवर्गीय जीवनका समग्र यथार्थलाई प्रस्तुत गरिएको छ । सर्वेक्षण, सूक्ष्म पठन तथा पाठ विश्लेषणको विधि प्रयोग गरी समग्रमा विश्लेषणात्मक विधिमार्फत सामान्यीकृत निष्कर्ष प्रस्तुत गरिएको ‘दसैँ’ र ‘सहीको सही’ कथामा सांस्कृतिक अध्ययन अन्तर्गत वर्गीय शक्तिसम्बन्धको खोजी र विश्लेषण गरिएको छ । यी कथामा उच्चवर्ग र निम्नवर्गबीचमा रहेको असमान, असन्तुलित र शत्रुतापूर्ण वर्गीय शक्तिसम्बन्धलाई देखाइएको छ । विश्लेष्य कथामा तत्कालीन समाजमा सामन्तवादी विमर्शात्मक संरचनायुक्त सञ्चेतना क्रियाशील रहेका कारण उत्पादनका साधनमाथि उच्चवर्गीय वर्चस्व कायम भएको छ र त्यसबाट निर्मित र प्रसारित ज्ञानका कारण वर्गीय शक्तिसम्बन्ध धमिलिई शत्रुतापूर्ण बनेको देखाइएको छ । तत्कालीन समाजमा उत्पादनका सबै साधनमाथि उच्चवर्गको वर्चस्व रहेको हुनाले वितरण प्रणाली र सामाजिक प्रभुत्वमा पनि उच्चवर्गकै आधिपत्य स्थापित भएको देखाइएको छ । यी कथामा वर्गीय विभेद, दमन र तत्कालीन समाज स्थापित सामन्ती ढाँचाको विमर्शात्मक संरचनाले उच्चवर्गलाई शासक र निम्नवर्गलाई शासितको स्थान तय गरिदिएर उच्चवर्गीय दमन, उत्पीडन र शोषणका लागि आधार तयार पारेको देखाइएको छ । तत्कालीन केन्द्रीय तथा स्थानीय सत्तामा सामन्तवादी उच्चवर्गकै वर्चस्व रहेका कारण निम्नवर्ग आवाजविहीन र निमुखो बन्न पुगेको देखिन्छ । त्यसै गरी केन्द्रीय सत्तासम्मको पहुँच समेत उच्चवर्गकै भएका कारण श्रमको मूल्य निर्धारण, सामाजिक न्याय, श्रमको अतिरिक्त मूल्यको शोषणजस्ता कार्यमा उच्चवर्गले छुट पाएको तथ्य निष्कर्षका रूपमा उक्त कथामा प्रस्तुत गरिएको छ ।
american_english: In the stories 'Dasain' and 'Sahi ko Sahi', collected in the story collection Gaunko Sandesh (2010), the thinking, outlook, character and conduct of the upper class and the lower class present in the society of that time, structured by feudalism, have been represented, and the whole reality of lower-class life has been presented. In 'Dasain' and 'Sahi ko Sahi', in which a generalized conclusion has been presented through an overall analytical method by using the methods of survey, close reading and textual analysis, the class power relationship has been sought out and analyzed under cultural studies. In these stories, the unequal, unbalanced and hostile class power relationship that exists between the upper class and the lower class has been shown. In the stories under analysis, because a consciousness structured by feudal discursive formation was active in the society of that time, upper-class dominance over the means of production was established, and it has been shown that, because of the knowledge produced and disseminated from that, the class power relationship grew blurred and became hostile. Since the upper class held dominance over all the means of production in the society of that time, it has been shown that the hegemony of the upper class was established also in the distribution system and in social dominance. In these stories, it has been shown that class discrimination, oppression and the discursive structure of the feudal pattern established in the society of that time fixed the place of the upper class as ruler and the lower class as ruled, preparing the ground for upper-class oppression, suppression and exploitation. Because the feudal upper class held dominance in the central and local power of that time, the lower class appears to have become voiceless and mute. Likewise, because access to central power as well was the upper class's own, the fact that the upper class got exemption in matters such as the fixing of the value of labor, social justice and the exploitation of the surplus value of labor has been presented in those stories as a conclusion.
british_english: In the stories 'Dasain' and 'Sahi ko Sahi', gathered in the short-story collection Gaunko Sandesh (2010), the thinking, outlook, character and conduct of the upper class and the lower class to be found in the society of the day, structured as it was by feudalism, have been represented, and the entire reality of lower-class life has been set forth. In 'Dasain' and 'Sahi ko Sahi', wherein a generalised conclusion has been set forth by way of an overall analytical method, the methods of survey, close reading and textual analysis having been employed, the class power relationship has been sought out and analysed within cultural studies. In these stories, the unequal, unbalanced and hostile class power relationship obtaining between the upper class and the lower class has been brought out. In the stories under analysis, inasmuch as a consciousness structured by feudal discursive formation was at work in the society of the day, upper-class dominance over the means of production was established, and it has been shown that, owing to the knowledge produced and disseminated out of it, the class power relationship was clouded over and turned hostile. Since the upper class held dominance over every means of production in the society of the day, it has been shown that the hegemony of the upper class was established in the distribution system and in social dominance as well. In these stories, it has been shown that class discrimination, oppression and the discursive structure of the feudal pattern established in the society of the day assigned to the upper class the position of ruler and to the lower class that of the ruled, thereby laying the ground for upper-class oppression, persecution and exploitation. Because the feudal upper class held dominance in the central and local authority of the day, the lower class is seen to have been left voiceless and mute. In like manner, because access to central authority too belonged to the upper class alone, the fact that the upper class was granted exemption in matters such as the fixing of the value of labour, social justice and the exploitation of the surplus value of labour has been set forth in those stories as a conclusion.
australian_english: In the stories 'Dasain' and 'Sahi ko Sahi' in the collection Gaunko Sandesh (2010), the thinking, outlook, character and behaviour of the upper class and the lower class in that old feudal-set-up society have been represented, and the whole reality of lower-class life has been put on show. Using survey, close reading and textual analysis, with a general conclusion offered through an overall analytical approach, 'Dasain' and 'Sahi ko Sahi' hunt down and analyse class power relations under cultural studies. These stories show up the unequal, unbalanced and outright hostile class power relations that sit between the upper class and the lower class. In the stories under the microscope, because a feudal-style consciousness was doing the rounds in that old society, the upper class got its grip on the means of production, and it is shown that the knowledge made and spread from there muddied the class power relationship and turned it hostile. Because the upper class held its grip on every means of production in that old society, it is shown that the upper class also called the shots in the distribution system and in social dominance. In these stories, it is shown that class discrimination, oppression and the feudal blueprints laid down in that old society chalked out the upper class as rulers and the lower class as the ruled, setting the stage for upper-class oppression, suppression and exploitation. Because the feudal upper class was holding sway in the central and local power of the day, the lower class comes across as having been left with no voice at all, just mute. In the same way, because even access to central power belonged to the upper class, the fact that the upper class got off scot-free on things like setting the value of labour, social justice and the exploitation of the surplus value of labour is put forward in those stories as a conclusion.

In the stories being looked at, because a feudal sort of thinking was doing the rounds in that old society, the upper class kept its grip on the means of production, and the knowledge made and spread from there muddied the class power relations and turned them hostile, that is what is shown. Because the upper class had its grip on every means of production in that old society, it is shown that the upper class also ran the distribution system and social dominance. translator_notes: "विमर्शात्मक संरचना" is rendered as "discursive formation/structure" in the standard theoretical sense. The abstract is one unbroken paragraph; sentence boundaries follow the Nepali, including the two long multi-clause sentences in the middle of the analysis.
